messages:
marta: Heads-up — us-west1 warm-pool is showing heavy fragmentation. Lots of tiny GPU pods (0.1-0.25 GPU) stuck pending on otherwise healthy nodes. Appears to be small-pod churn + binpacking gap.

xiang: saw that earlier, cluster metrics show ~60% of GPUs have tiny leftover slices that are unusable for our 1-GPU tasks.

marta: alert fired: `scheduler.eviction_rate > 200/min` and `gpu_utilization_per_node < 0.35` despite high pending queue.

deploy-bot: Incident created #INC-5932 — High pod pending due to GPU slot fragmentation in us-west1. Assigned: @sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: I’m looking. Quick dump: `kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, gpus: .status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu, pods: (.status.capacity.pods - .status.allocatable.pods)}'` — will paste node summary in a sec.

chris: FYI this started after the warm-pool scale-up yesterday (autoscaler bumped by 12 nodes). My bet: new nodes came with tiny leftover allocatable due to pod overhead and our pod requests are fractional which triggers scatter.

marta: can we try an immediate workaround: enable soft-evict for tiny pods and backfill them into warm-pool nodes with a temporary binpack policy? or bump fractional rounding to 0.5 for the short term?

xiang: we can also try packing policy `packd = "microbin"` (experimental) — it groups tiny pods into co-scheduled micro-gangs to reduce fragmentation. Needs a short rollout and we should gate by az.

chris: agree with gating. Risk: might increase preemption for larger jobs. Suggest: rollout in us-west1a only and flip back if eviction noise spikes.

marta: cost question — if we leave it, we end up with inflated node count and wasted GPU-hours. Estimate: ~18% wasted gpu-hours on the pool last 24h => ~$2.3k/day.

tara: can we also try increase warm-pool lifetime and prefer draining older nodes first? Warm-pool churn seems to create many 0.2-GPU leftovers after daemonsets land.

xiang: good call. Sequence to try now: 1) increase warm-pool min-lifetime to 30m, 2) apply packd microbin to us-west1a (canary), 3) enable soft-evict policy for pods with label `tiny=true` and grace 60s.

sre-oncall: doing step 1 now. Patching autoscaler config. Will monitor.

deploy-bot: autoscaler config patched by @sre-oncall (change-id: cfg-8043).

marta: after that, if fragmentation persists, we should consider a short-lived binpack job that triggers `kubectl drain --packed` style migration for tiny pods to co-locate them (non-preemptive migration). That will require maintenance window.

chris: noted — I can prep the migration job and a rollback plan. Also adding a metric for "micro-fragmentation" (count of fractional leftover <0.5 GPU per node) so we can alert earlier.

tara: one more thing — audit daemonsets and node-affinity hooks. Some infra DS are requesting fractional GPUs for profiling sidecars; we should tighten those.

marta: thanks. If packd microbin looks stable in canary (30m), we’ll expand. Track: pending count, eviction rate, wasted GPU-hours, and preemptions.

xiang: rolling packd canary to us-west1a now (feature-flag: packd.microbin=true).

deploy-bot: Feature flag packd.microbin=true enabled in us-west1a by @xiang (ff-id: ff-2107).

sre-oncall: packd canary up. Initial observations: pending queue dropped ~28% in 6m, eviction rate down a bit. Watching preemptions.

marta: good early signal. Keep this thread for updates. If anyone hits a regression, @mention here and toggle ff off. :thumbsup:
